- When sentiment is strongly positive (≥0.8) and forecast is rising sharply, reduce overshoot by 5–10% to avoid overcorrection.  
- If sentiment is negative (≤0.2) and forecast is falling, avoid premature bottoming — delay downward correction by 1–2 periods.  
- After a sharp price spike (forecast > true +10%), apply a “mean reversion” penalty: subtract 2–3% from next period’s forecast.  
- If sentiment is neutral (0.2–0.8) and forecast deviates >5% from true, adjust toward recent 7-day average to reduce lag bias.  
- For 30-day horizons, if true outcome is consistently below forecast (e.g., 3+ consecutive days), reduce forecast by 1–2% per period to reflect underestimation bias.  
- If sentiment history shows repeated “reversal” patterns (e.g., 2+ consecutive high/low sentiment), apply a “sentiment decay” rule: reduce forecast sensitivity to sentiment by 30% in next 3 periods.
